sources.text: Researcher · Educator · Entrepreneur Edward Jay Wang I build point-of-need medical technologies — bioengineering and design research that creates medical-grade physiological measurements where health concerns actually arise. Associate Professor, UC San Diego — ECE & Human Centered Design Jacobs Faculty Chair in Entrepreneurship CEO & Founder, Billion Labs Inc. Curriculum Vitae DigiHealth Lab ↗ Billion Labs ↗ 43 publications · 9 paper awards NIH Trailblazer Award NAE Frontiers of Engineering Speaker Google Research Faculty Fellow Norman Foundation Design Laureate NSF Graduate Research Fellow Background 2026 Visiting Associate Professor Stanford University · Bioengineering 2025 – Present Associate Professor with Tenure UC San Diego · ECE & Human Centered Design 2019 – 2025 Assistant Professor (Tenure Track) UC San Diego · ECE & Human Centered Design 2013 – 2019 PhD, Electrical & Computer Engineering University of Washington 2015 Academic Researcher Microsoft Research 2014 Academic Researcher Intel Corporation 2012 Researcher, Human-Computer Interaction Hasso Plattner Institute 2008 – 2012 BS, General Engineering (Bioengineering) Harvey Mudd College Publications Point-of-need is distinct from both clinical point-of-care and consumer wellness tracking. The clinic is where care is delivered; the wrist is where convenience lives. Point-of-need is the moment and place a health question first surfaces — at home, at work, in the field — and the goal is to put a measurement of clinical quality into that moment without requiring a clinic to be there. My group works this problem along three complementary lines: designing the sensing artifacts themselves, understanding how a technology is actually adopted in real-world contexts, and developing design principles that hold across diverse populations rather than only the people who happen to resemble the design team.
